(p-73) Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn

Its purpose is the complete warning against what corrupts faith (īmān) among inward deeds, and the admonition against what harms Islam among outward states, through the contradiction between action and speech. For this is hypocrisy (nifāq) in general, and it is about to draw one to full hypocrisy, so that one leaves the religion and enters the abyss (al-Hāwiyah). The purpose of this warning is that it be a cause of truthfulness in speech, then truthfulness in deeds, then truthfulness in character, then truthfulness in states, and then the guarding of one's breaths. The truthfulness of speech is that the speaker says nothing except on the basis of proof (burhān). The truthfulness of deeds is that innovation (bid'ah) has no authority over them. The truthfulness of character is that one does not regard the goodness that appears from oneself, after exaggerating it, except with the eye of deficiency. The truthfulness of states is that they be based on unveiling and clarity. The truthfulness of breaths is that one breathes only with a presence like direct witnessing. Naming them "the hypocrites" is clear in this regard. [Begin with] "In the name of Allah" (bismillāh), to whom belongs the greatest encompassing in knowledge and power; so whoever deviates, He intends for him, [and] "the Most Merciful" (al-Raḥmān), who by the generality of His mercy covers whomever He wills of His servants, and exposes whomever He wills, even if he refines his deception and conceals it; [and] "the Most Compassionate" (al-Raḥīm), who grants success to the people of His love by completing His favour for what He loves and is pleased with.

(p-74)

When He, glory be to Him, forbade in Sūrat al-Mumtaḥanah the taking of His enemy as an ally, and censured in Sūrat al-Ṣaff the contradiction between speech and action, and warned at the end of Sūrat al-Jumu'ah against turning away from any state of the Prophet (ﷺ) in favour of another state, even with agreement, because the form of all of that is the form of hypocrisy, He mentioned at the beginning of this [sūrah] the condition of those who approached him in the state of hypocrisy, for such a person is like the Jews who were charged with the Torah and then did not bear it. The sūrah continues in censuring them with the worst censure, so that it may serve as a deterrent against everything whose outward appearance is hypocrisy. Thus the Exalted said: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you﴾, i.e., O Messenger, who is announced in the Torah and the Gospel; ﴿the hypocrites﴾, i.e., those who are firmly established in the attribute of hypocrisy, which is outward Islam and inward disbelief, and most of them are from the Jews; ﴿they say﴾, emphasising [their words] because they sense that the one listening to them may disbelieve them, given the doubt they harbour: ﴿"We bear witness"﴾. Al-Ḥasan said: it has the status of an oath, as if they had said, "We swear." ﴿"Indeed you"﴾, the emphasis for this and [its] suggestion, because of the intensity of their emphasis due to their great desire for the content of what they say: ﴿"are surely the Messenger of Allah"﴾, i.e., the King who has complete encompassing. Thus they agreed with the truth in their outward states, and opposed it in their hearts and actions.

(p-75)

Since testimony (shahādah) is the report based on certain knowledge, for it derives from witnessing (shuhūd), which is the completeness of presence and the totality of awareness, and the agreement of the hearts with the tongues, Allah, glory be to Him, confirmed the thing testified to and denied them in their swearing by testimony, and in the agreement of their tongues with their hearts. He said: ﴿And Allah knows﴾, i.e., His knowledge is knowledge in reality. He, glory be to Him, emphasised this in accordance with the denial of the hypocrites, and said: ﴿that you are surely His Messenger﴾, whether or not the hypocrites testify to that. So the testimony to it is true from one whose tongue agrees with his heart. This was placed between their testimony and their denial, lest it be imagined that what their testimony contained of the message was a lie.

Since it may be thought that this is an emphasis of the words of the hypocrites, He indicated that it is a verification of the content of their words, not of their testimony, and so said: ﴿And Allah﴾, i.e., the One encompassing all attributes of perfection, ﴿bears witness﴾, a testimony which is the testimony [because it encompasses] the subtleties of the outward and inward; ﴿that the hypocrites﴾, i.e., those firmly established in the attribute of hypocrisy, ﴿are surely liars﴾, i.e., in their report about themselves that they bear witness, because their hearts do not agree with their tongues, so they do not believe that. Among the conditions of speaking the truth is that its outward match its inward, and its secret match its public [expression]. Whenever this is not the case, it is a lie. It is not meant that they are liars regarding the soundness of what their testimony contains, that you are the Messenger of Allah.

(p-76)

The summary is that testimony contains two things: the truth of the content of the report, and assent to it. Their truthfulness is in the first, and their lying in the second. Thus, through their hypocrisy, they became lower in condition and worse in end than the Jews.

Imam Abū Ja'far Ibn al-Zubayr said: When the state of the believers in what Allah singled them out with, of what the three verses comprised up to the beginning of Sūrat al-Jumu'ah, up to His saying ﴿And Allah is the possessor of great bounty﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 4], was followed by mention of the state of those who did not benefit from what they were charged with, as was previously explained, and there was in that admonitions and warnings which those whom happiness had preceded would benefit from, He followed it with what is more striking to the purpose and more eloquent in aim: the mention of a group among them, who had been praised earlier, and among their peers, their kin and their relatives, who appeared outwardly in faith, showed submission and assent, and then were confronted and turned away, and dissociated themselves from what they had reached; rather, destinies hindered them, so that insight and sight became blind. It is well known and consistent that a person's admonition by those closest to him and by the people of his own time is more prevalent than his admonition by those distant from him in time and lineage. So Sūrat al-Jumu'ah was followed by Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn as an admonition to the believers through the condition of the people of hypocrisy, and it expounded some of their stories that fit what we have mentioned. It had been said to them: "Those who showed submission and acceptance are not [better]..., then the Children of Israel, then [there was] in what was charged to them like the donkey carrying books, [being] more wondrous than the state of your brothers in time and kinship, while you are the most knowledgeable of people (p-77) about them, and that they had been described in the pre-Islamic age (al-jāhiliyyah) as having good judgement and sound insight."

﴿And when you see them, their bodies please you, and if they speak you listen to their speech﴾ [al-Munāfiqūn: 4]. ﴿But the hypocrites do not understand﴾ [al-Munāfiqūn: 7].

I say: What we narrated in the Muṣannaf of Ibn Abī Shaybah has already passed in the khuṭbah, from the words of some believers: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite in the Friday [prayer] Sūrat al-Jumu'ah and al-Munāfiqūn," so he gladdened the believers with it and encouraged them; as for Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn, he made the hypocrites despair with it and rebuked them. This is similar to what we mentioned first. The end.

When the meaning was that they did not believe what they testified to, and it was as if it were said: "What drives them to this emphatic speech and to a lie that is extremely ugly, especially among the Arabs?", he explained it by His saying, naming their testimony as faith (īmān), because testimony functions as an oath in intending emphasis; for this reason it is introduced with what an oath is introduced with: ﴿They have taken﴾, i.e., they took with their utmost effort, ﴿their oaths﴾, i.e., all of them, from this testimony of theirs, striving to confirm it, and every other oath besides it, ﴿as a shield﴾, i.e., a protection that guards them from worldly harms, and they hide behind it from them, so they safeguard by it their blood and their wealth. They sought illumination from the light of acceptance, but the ray of the light of felicity did not spread over them, so their light was extinguished by the domination of deprivation, and they remained in the darknesses of the previously decreed portion by the judgment of abandonment. ﴿So they barred﴾, i.e., their taking of this caused them to turn away themselves, together with the evil of their inner selves (p-78) and the heat of their breasts, and they led others to turn away, because of what they saw of their evil states through those outward appearances, while they remained upon the disbelief to which they had become accustomed, which Satan adorns for them, ﴿from the way of Allah﴾, i.e., from the path of the Supreme King which He legislated for His servants so that they might reach through it the station of His good pleasure. They reached that through their deception and their scheming, with their boldness in false oaths by which they walk in their affairs, in contrast to what Allah legislated in this tolerant, easy monotheism concerning the reliance upon the oath-taker's own oath regarding matters that no one knows except from his side.

Since what He reported of their condition is extremely ugly, it produced His saying: ﴿Indeed they﴾, and He emphasized it because their state is strange to them, and many marvel at those who draw near to them, ﴿evil is what they used to do﴾, i.e., by nature and disposition, ﴿they were doing﴾, i.e., they were renewing their deed, persisting in it with what is almost innate, through their boldness toward Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, and He saved His servants by the false oaths.

This is the commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 63, verse 3:

When sins blind the heart, how much more so the greatest of them. He gives the reason for this in His words: ﴿That﴾, meaning the great matter of being far from good, namely lying by reporting testimony and swearing to the truth, barring from the way, and describing their deeds as evil, ﴿because they believed﴾, meaning because they professed belief with their tongues without their hearts corresponding to it. Since disbelief is considered unlikely, how much more so when it comes after professing faith, He expresses this with the particle of distance (dhalika), and so that the blame for backsliding is understood a fortiori (min bab al-awla, "by way of what is more fitting"). Also, so that one does not suppose that the blame applies only to the reversion from faith to disbelief and not to disbelief in general. (p-79) Thus the expression with "then" (thumma) indicates that whoever persisted in faith all his life and then disbelieved a moment before his death incurs this blame. So He says: ﴿then they disbelieved﴾, meaning secretly, so they feared people and did not fear God. Since mere sealing of the heart is extremely abominable, it implies a fortiori the abomination of what came from God, so the verb is put in the passive: His words ﴿so they were sealed﴾, meaning the sealing (tab') occurred, namely the stamping (khatm), although it is known that no one other than Him, glorified is He, is able to do that, ﴿upon their hearts﴾, because of their audacity in committing what is the greatest of the major sins, in the manner of hypocrisy, until they became accustomed to disbelief and became firmly established in it. Likewise, whoever abandons the Friday prayer three times out of negligence. ﴿Therefore they﴾, meaning as a consequence of that, ﴿do not understand﴾, meaning no understanding occurs to them regarding anything at all, so they cannot distinguish right from wrong or truth from falsehood, because nothing reaches what is sealed, and nothing comes out of it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 63, verse 4:

When He, glory be to Him, described their inner selves, by which He showed disdain for them (because a person is by his intellect, just as the food is by its form), and they had appearances that deceived the beholder (for the Arabs used to say: "Beauty of appearance generally indicates goodness of what is reported"), He said, exalted is He: ﴿And when you see them﴾, that is, O Messenger, with the insight and penetrating perception you possess, or O beholder, whoever he may be, with the eye of sight, ﴿their bodies impress you﴾ for their largeness and comeliness. For their whole aim is only the soundness of their outward appearances and the enjoyment of their selves. They are mere forms and shapes, with no intellects or realities behind them. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Ibn Ubayy [i.e., the one because of whom the surah was revealed] was large-bodied, eloquent, healthy, and sharp-tongued, and a group of hypocrites were of a similar description, and they were the leaders of Madinah. They used to attend the gathering of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and lean upon it, and they had imposing presence and eloquent tongues. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and those present used to be impressed by their physiques. When He had described the inner and outer states, and their saying was: "A man is by his two smaller parts, his heart and his tongue," which is conditional, as the apparent wording shows, on the agreement of the tongue with the heart, He said, expressing it with the particle of doubt, indicating that they speak to him (ﷺ) only under compulsion, because they do not love conversing with him and have no motive for it due to the diseases of their hearts: ﴿And if they speak﴾, that is, there issues from them speech at some time or other, ﴿you listen to their speech﴾, that is, because it is such that it delights the hearing and pleases the mind, due to the flattery it contains along with eloquence, so it seizes the totality of the heart.

When He reported about their outward state, He indicated that this outward appearance is something without reality, and that, since they had accustomed themselves to shamelessness and cast off the garment of modesty through falsehood, they expended all effort in embellishing speech, because they think there is no reckoning against them in it in any respect, for they do not reckon with the Hereafter. So He said: ﴿As if they﴾, that is, in the goodness of their outward appearances and the badness of their inner states, and in cowardice and feebleness, and in their being of no benefit in anything of understanding or steadfastness, for they have no reality, ﴿are logs﴾, a plural of paucity... no, a plural of multitude of "khashabah" (a piece of wood), and this is evidence of their multitude. Since wood may sometimes be applied to what is planted, He negated that by His saying, emphasizing the multitude by the doubling of the letter: ﴿propped up﴾, that is, they have been cut from their planting places, peeled, and propped against walls so that the soil does not spoil them. So they are white, dazzling the wonder of the beholder, yet without steadfastness, without fruit within, and without water, so there is no heavenly supply [for them] at all that purifies them with any kind of growth. They have lost the spirit of affirmation by which their perfection lies, just as the hypocrite has lost the spirit of faith by which the perfection and continuance of the speaker lies. Thus in that state they are shapes without spirits, bodies without minds.

Since whoever says what he does not do becomes suspected by everyone who speaks to him, for by breaking his word he has become his enemy, so people all imagine themselves to be his enemies, and this brings him the greatest cowardice, and that is the greatest cause of the embellishment of his speech. He said: ﴿They think﴾, that is, because of the weakness of their intellects and the abundance of their doubt, due to the abundance of the evil deeds they commit, ﴿every shout﴾, that is, from the call of a caller regarding a beast that has escaped or the proclaiming of a lost thing, and the like, ﴿against them﴾, that is, falling upon them. Since whoever thinks people are hostile to him will himself be hostile to them, He said, as a conclusion of what has passed: ﴿They are﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿the enemy﴾, that is, the complete enemy, by what the report indicates through the singular noun that applies to the plural, rather than the plural, indicating that they, in the intensity of their enmity toward Islam and its people, and the completeness of their intent and the intensity of their striving in it, are of one heart, even if they show affection in speech and closeness to the people of Islam, for their tongues are with you when they meet you, while their hearts are against you with your enemies. So they are spies for them against you.

When He explained this about their bad states, He made the following a consequence of it: ﴿So beware of them﴾, because the worst of enemies is the enemy who flatters you while under his ribs lies a grievous disease. Whoever senses that you are his enemy will plot harms against you, and most who please you with speech on this description will be so, but by Allah's kindness he will be constantly defeated and overturned in most of his vicissitudes, in the hand of compulsion and deprivation, owing to the secret of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿May Allah destroy them﴾, that is, may the King, encompassing in knowledge and power, place them in the position of one who is fought by a mighty enemy who fights him most fiercely, according to the custom of an act that occurs between two.

When their condition was most astonishing in their turning away from Islam, first by blindness to the manifest signs, and second by refusing to report their secrets and the hidden nature of their deceit and their news, and in their not being turned away from the ugliness of their inner states and the evil of their consciences, by the inversion of their aims and the frustration of their sources and destinations in their deception, He indicated this by His saying: ﴿How are they turned away?﴾, that is, how and from what direction, ﴿are they turned away﴾, that is, some turner turns them away from perceiving the ugliness of what they are upon, whatever that turner may be, so that they might return from it to the goodness of the religion, to finding comfort in it, to perceiving its blessing and its great effect.

When this was a grave matter that cuts them off from God and His Messenger, its perpetrator would urgently need purification. Given its gravity, it was fitting that it would not be fully purified except by asking the Prophet (ﷺ) to pray for forgiveness. Since they did not do this, it shows the corruption of their inner selves, the hardness of their hearts, and that they were like propped-up pieces of wood, having no fruit and no growth at all. This is expressed in His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them﴾ [i.e., by whatever speaker it is said]: ﴿come﴾, i.e., raise yourselves up, striving toward this by coming to the most noble of creation, whose place remains high because of the loftiness of his station. ﴿the Messenger of God will ask forgiveness for you﴾, i.e., he will seek forgiveness on your behalf specifically, after you have turned away from your sin, the sin of this lie to which you persist. Since the preceding verb has two governors, he gave the second of them the function (of governing), as is the preferred view of the Basran grammarians, so he put ﴿the Messenger of God﴾ in the nominative, i.e., the nearest of creation to the Greatest King, whose generosity has no equal. ﴿they twist their heads﴾ [i.e., they do], twisting with the utmost intensity and frequency, which is turning away in another direction, out of aversion, arrogance, and a display of hatred and repulsion. They exaggerated in this in a way that shows they are overpowered by it, because of the intensity of the sickness within their inner selves. ﴿and you see them﴾, i.e., with the eye of insight, ﴿turning away﴾, i.e., turning away in an ugly manner from what they were called to, repeatedly doing so every time they are called. The clause is in the position of the second object of "you see". ﴿while they are arrogant﴾, i.e., persistently proud regarding what they were called to, and regarding placing themselves in a position of seeking excuse. Because of the severity of their hardness, they do not perceive the ugliness of what they are upon, nor are they guided to its cure. When others guide them and warn them, they are not warned. It is narrated that when the Qur'an was revealed concerning them, their tribesmen from among the believers came to them and said: "Woe to you! You have disgraced yourselves and destroyed yourselves. Go to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), turn to him, and ask him to pray for forgiveness for you." But they refused. So God revealed this verse. It is also narrated that Ibn Ubayy, their leader, twisted his head and said to them: "You advised me to believe, so I believed; you advised me to give the zakat of my wealth, so I gave it. Nothing remains except that you order me to prostrate to Muhammad."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 63, verse 6:

Since the Prophet (ﷺ) desired their well-being, he desired to seek forgiveness for them, and perhaps some of their relatives urged him to do so. So his seeking forgiveness was of the kind in which he would ask about it. He said, [drawing attention] to the fact that they are not worthy of forgiveness because they do not believe.

﴿It is the same for them﴾: that is, this equality, which they struggled within themselves to attain until they took it on as a character trait, prevailed and dominated, so that it became free of the slightest inclination or effort, ﴿upon them﴾.

Since in this context the interrogative meaning had been stripped from the hamza, the meaning of ﴿Whether you ask forgiveness for them﴾, that is, at this time, ﴿or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾, that is, in it or in what comes after, is: your seeking forgiveness for them and your leaving it are equal in their eyes, because it has no effect on them. For this reason, its outcome, as a punishment upon them, is the emphatic negation in His saying: ﴿Allah will never forgive them﴾, that is, the Supreme King ﴿them﴾. Perhaps the expression by means of the interrogative after its meaning has been stripped away is to indicate that if they were to witness the King asking you about that, it would not turn them back from their hypocrisy, and it would add nothing whatsoever to what they already have. The Prophet (ﷺ) had restricted this verse by the verse of Bara'ah, which allows for choice, and that if he exceeded seventy, forgiveness would be hoped for. Thus he deemed it permissible, on that basis, to pray over Ibn Ubayy, the leader of the hypocrites, and to ask forgiveness for him, because of the [great] compassion that he (ﷺ) had toward the servants of Allah and his abundant mercy toward them, especially whoever was among his Companions and the Ansar, may Allah be pleased with them (p-86), [with special] care for him.

Since the intended sense was to give the reason for the emphasis in the statement after the forgiveness for them, namely: because their wickedness had become firmly established so that it became a settled attribute of theirs, he expressed this by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses the attributes of perfection, ﴿does not guide the people﴾, that is, the people who have strength within themselves to do what they wish, ﴿the defiantly disobedient﴾, because they have no excuse for persisting in defiant disobedience, which is to exit the fortress of Islam by breaching and tearing it again and again and practicing it until it became firmly established. Thus they are deeply rooted in hypocrisy and far removed from the prospect of reform.

When this [statement] prompted the question about the matter over which they had transgressed, He said, clarifying it: ﴿They are the ones who say﴾, that is, they are the ones who originated this saying and never cease to renew it. This is because they were bound to the secondary causes (asbab), veiled from witnessing the divine decree (taqdir), and not truly realizing that affairs are governed by God's directing of judgments. What had taken root in their hearts, the wish to extinguish the light of God, made them speak, so they enjoined one another with their words: ﴿Do not spend﴾, O believers who sincerely aid [the Prophet], ﴿on those﴾, that is, those who ﴿are with the Messenger of God﴾, that is, the King who encompasses everything. They were the poor among the Emigrants. They expressed it this way while not believing it, as mockery and as an implication that if His Messenger, who is absolute wealth, [were truly his Messenger], he would enrich his companions and would not leave them in need of people spending on them. The foolish did not realize that this was a trial from Him, glorified is He, for His servants, ﴿so glory be to Him who leads astray whom He wills﴾, until their speech became the furthest thing from correctness, such that the intelligent person is astonished at how such a thing could come from anyone. Or else these were not their words, which is the apparent reading. God, glorified is He, expressed it this way about them to indicate that their speech amounts to willing harm from God against him, as a rebuke for their disbelief and an alert that whoever sends a messenger does not leave him to anyone, but suffices him in everything that concerns him, without any need at all. God, glorified is He, had sent to him, peace be upon him, the keys to the treasuries of the earth, but he refused them. This madness did not satisfy them; they added to it what shows that they thought the doors of provision close when people who spend refuse to spend. They used a particle of limit (ghayah), so that what follows it takes the ruling of what precedes it, and said: ﴿until they disperse﴾, that is, scatter in a shameful manner involving breaking up, so that each of them goes off to his family and to the business he had before that. Al-Harrali said: "Hatta" is a word that conveys a bounded limit, in which what follows enters into the ruling of what precedes it, in contrast to the meaning of "ila" (to). The grammarians of Arabic said: it does not carry [the sense of limit] to something other, or to something connected with the other, such as "al-fajr" in ﴿until the rising of dawn﴾ [al-Qadr: 5], and "until the end of the night." Do not say "until the middle of the night." The boorish did not realize that if they had done this, God would have brought others to be hypocrites instead, or He would have commanded His Messenger, peace be upon him, so that he supplicated over a small amount and it became abundant, or it was of a kind that would not run out, [or He gave each one a small portion of food in a manner that would not run out], as with the dates of Abu Hurayrah, the barley of 'A'ishah, and the ghee of Umm Ayman, may God be pleased with them all, and other such accounts, as has been related on more than one occasion. But there is no guide for whom God leads astray. For this reason, in refuting them He said: ﴿And to God belongs﴾, that is, they said that [saying] and persisted in renewing it, while the truth is that to the King, with whom no one has any command, belongs the authority to command and forbid. ﴿The treasuries of the heavens﴾ [all of them] ﴿and of the earth﴾, likewise, of things that do not yet exist, which fall under His power, ﴿His command is only that when He wills a thing, He says to it "Be," and it is﴾ (Yasin: 82). And of the things He has brought into existence, He gives to whom He wills what He wills, even from their own hands. No one can prevent any of that, neither from what is in his own hand nor from what is in the hand of another. He drew attention to the badness of their dullness and that they had shackled themselves to illusion until they fell from the rank of the beasts, as one of them said: "If Muhammad is truthful, then we are worse than the beasts." He alluded to this with His words: ﴿But the hypocrites﴾, that is, those deeply rooted in the description of hypocrisy.

Since what is conveyed to creatures of provision leads many of them to think they obtained it by their own strength, He expressed it with the more specific sense of knowledge (fiqh), saying: ﴿do not understand﴾, that is (p. 89), no understanding is ever renewed for them at all. This is because beasts, when they see something that benefits them in a place on some day, seek it there again another time. These people saw, more than once, the extraordinary blessings God produced at the hand of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, yet that did not benefit them. Whoever sees that his provision is in the hand of creatures, and that this diverts him from God until he neglects His rights and compromises in his religion, has disassociated himself from the Qur'an. He indicated their lack of understanding with His words, exalted is He: [continuing with the next verse]

﴿They say﴾, that is, they originate this statement and repeat it, emphasizing it because they sense that most of their people deny it: ﴿If we return﴾, that is, [we, O you hypocritical group], from this raid of ours, in which they saw from the victory of the Prophet ﷺ what defies description. This was the raid of Banu al-Mustaliq, a clan of Hudhayl, at al-Muraysi', which is a water source of theirs on the side of Qudayd toward the coast. In it Ibn Ubayy spoke the slander (al-ifk) and spread it. ﴿to Medina﴾ [and] they indicated their determination not to remain in company with the believers by their saying: ﴿the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it﴾, meaning themselves by "the mightier," and the believers by "the meaner." They are lying in this, but out of their extreme dullness they imagined that might belongs to them and that they were able to expel the believers. ﴿But to Allah belongs﴾, that is, while the case is that everyone who has any measure of insight knows that to the Supreme King, who alone possesses the might of divinity, belongs ﴿all the might﴾; He is the Subduer over whoever is below Him, and everything other than Him is below Him.

[p. 90] When He restricted might to what indicated this through the fronting of the object (taqdim al-ma'mul), He informed that He gives of it to whomever He wills, and the most deserving of it are those who obey Him. He expressed this in His saying: ﴿and to His Messenger﴾, because his might derives from His might, through the might of prophethood and messengership and Allah's making His religion prevail over all religions. Likewise, might belongs to whoever obeys the Messenger, in His saying: ﴿and to the believers﴾, that is, those for whom faith has become an enduring attribute, because their might is through the might of allegiance (al-wilayah). Allah granted them victory as a might for their Messenger ﷺ, and whoever seeks might through Allah will not be touched by humiliation.

Since their ignorance in this was greater, given how much they had seen of Allah's support for His Messenger ﷺ and for whoever followed him, may Allah be pleased with them, and of their elevation over everyone who opposed them, He said, alerting to this: ﴿But the hypocrites do not know﴾, that is, those in whom the sickness of the hearts has become firmly established.

Since the proofs of Allah's might are not hidden from anyone, because of what has been established of His subjugation of kings and others by death, from which no one could escape or contend, and of His prevention of most desires, and of His destroying the enemies of the Messenger and his followers with various kinds of destruction, and that He, glory be to Him, never said anything without it coming to pass, nor did the Messengers say anything without Him confirming it, He concluded the verse with knowledge in its more general sense (al-'ilm al-a'amm) from jurisprudence (al-fiqh), saying: ﴿do not know﴾, that is, they have no knowledge at all now, nor will it be renewed [p. 91] at any time whatsoever. Therefore they say such idle nonsense (al-kharaf). It is narrated that when this verse was revealed, 'Abdullah, the son of 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, whose father was the reason for its revelation, came to his father during the raid of al-Muraysi' against Banu al-Mustaliq, seized the rein of his father's she-camel, and said: "By Allah, you are the meaner, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the mightier." When they drew near the honored city of Medina, he drew his sword, came to his father, seized the rein of his she-camel, and drove it back, saying: "Stay back! By Allah, you will not enter it until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gives permission. And if you do not acknowledge that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the mightier and you are the meaner, I will strike your neck!" He said: "Are you going to do it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "I bear witness that might belongs to Allah, to His Messenger, and to the believers." He complained of his son to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger ordered that he be allowed to enter Medina, so he was released and entered.

[p-92] Since what Allah, glorified and exalted be He, relates about the hypocrites is such that one is astonished beyond measure that anyone could even conceive of it, let alone utter it, much less believe it, He draws attention to the cause that necessitates it: the blinding of insight. The cause of this blinding of insight is turning one's whole heart toward this world. This is a return to clarifying what was said earlier in the commentary on the Friday prayer [in] (p-92) the permission to seek provision and the warning against acts like that of Hatib, may Allah be pleased with him, and the act of those who turned away from the sermon toward that [caravan]. This admonition was given in a decisive manner, to cut off the source of their evil in speech, for the word of stinginess [as it is said] is obeyed, whether it has some effect or causes some degree of restraint at some time. So He said, calling out to those who need this: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, meaning: inform them of what requires that their inner selves submit as their outer selves do. ﴿Let not your wealth distract you﴾. Since the address is to those who need emphasis, He said: ﴿or your children﴾, meaning: do not turn your whole hearts toward any of these in a way that bewilders you, whether that is in its improvement or in enjoying it, such that you become occupied and heedless ﴿of the remembrance of Allah﴾, meaning of the monotheism of the Supreme King, who has complete encompassment over everything, to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs praise, He gives to whom He wills and withholds from whom He wills. When the servant remembers Him constantly in his heart, he will not say, as the hypocrites said, ﴿Do not spend﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 7], nor ﴿Surely the more honorable will expel the more humble from it﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8], because he knows that the whole affair belongs to Allah, and that he will never harm Allah in any way, and that he harms only himself by that. This includes what they said about monotheism, prayer, pilgrimage, fasting and other things. And for the sake of emphasis in the prohibition, the prohibition was directed at wealth and children, while what is actually meant is the prohibition of people. (p-93) Since the implied meaning is: whoever desists, he is among the successful, the following was joined to it: ﴿And whoever does that﴾, meaning [commits] at any time, in a continual and persistent manner, the act of ﴿that﴾, that is, the matter far removed from the deeds of people of high aspiration, namely devoting oneself to busying oneself with what is perishable, turning away from what remains, turning toward the immediate while forgetting the hereafter. ﴿Then those﴾, meaning those far removed from good, ﴿they are﴾, meaning specifically, ﴿the losers﴾, meaning the utterly ruined in loss, to the extent that it is as if they were singled out for it over other people. This is the opposite of what they intended by looking after their own interests and turning toward them with striving for increase, growth and gain. In its implication is that whoever is occupied by what concerns him of the matters of his religion, which Allah, glorified be He, commanded him to do and forbade him from, and whose neglect He threatened, Allah, glorified be He, will suffice him in the matter of his worldly life, which He has guaranteed him, and will forbid him from making it his greatest concern, and will threaten him for that. Thus, none remembers Him except one who finds Him in all his affairs, religious and worldly, turns to Him in all his calamities, devotes all his cares to Him, and gives himself to Him as one who knows that he is a owned and nurtured servant. He has entrusted his soul to his Lord and taken Him as Disposer of affairs, so he is at rest from fears and does not incline to any of the greedy desires, and thus he becomes free.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 63, verse 10:

When he had warned against turning toward this world, he encouraged spending from it, in opposition to the hypocrites, and so he said: ﴿And spend﴾, meaning from what you have been commanded to give, whether obligatory or recommended. He added to the encouragement by making pleased acceptance from them easy, even though all of it belongs to Him, through his saying: ﴿from what We have provided you﴾, meaning from Our greatness. He reached the final limit in this by being pleased to act on what He commanded, together with sincere repentance (tawbah nasuh), at some time, even if it is little, by what the affirmation of the preposition (al-jarr, the particle "min") points to. He said, encouraging preparation for departure and hastening to meet the appointed term (ajal) suddenly, warning against being deceived by postponement during times of safety: ﴿before﴾, and he unpacked the verbal noun (masdar) so that "anna" (that) would convey greater nearness, [so he said]: ﴿that there come﴾. Since placing the object first, as already mentioned in al-Nisa', is more frightening, he said: ﴿death to one of you﴾, [meaning] by seeing its signs and indications, and every moment that passes is one of its signs and indications. Since hardships require turning toward God, he made that the consequence by his saying: ﴿then he says﴾, asking for a return, and he indicated its softening of hearts by his saying: ﴿My Lord, why did You not﴾, meaning, "Is there not, and why not," ﴿delay me﴾, meaning delay my death as a respite for me, ﴿to a term﴾, meaning a period of time. He made clear that his purpose is only to make up what he missed, by his saying: ﴿a short term, so that I may give charity﴾, meaning in order to provision myself for this long journey that I am about to undertake.

Al-Ghazali said in the Book of Repentance from the Ihya' (Revival of the Religious Sciences): One of the gnostics (arifin) said: When the Angel of Death appears to the servant, he informs him that only an hour of your life remains, and that you will not be delayed from it even for the blink of an eye. Then there appears in the servant such regret and anguish that, if the whole world were his, he would give it all to add to that hour another hour in which he could make amends and make up for his negligence. He says: "O Angel of Death! Postpone me one day, in which I may apologize to my Lord, repent, and provision myself with righteousness for my soul." [The Angel] says: "The hours have run out, so there is no hour left." Then the door of repentance is closed upon him, and he chokes on his soul, his breaths rattle in his chest, and he swallows the bitterness of despair of making amends and the anguish of regret over squandering his life. The root of his faith trembles under the shocks of those terrors. When his soul departs, if the Most Beautiful [decree] from God had preceded for him, his soul departs in tawhid (monotheism), and that is a good end (husn al-khatimah). But if the decree of wretchedness had preceded for him, and God forbid, his soul departs in doubt and turmoil, and that is a bad end (su' al-khatimah). Whoever leaves the hastening to repentance by procrastination stands between two great dangers: first, that darkness accumulates on his heart from sins until it becomes rust and a seal, and then it does not accept erasure; second, that illness or death overtakes him and he finds no respite to occupy himself with erasure, so God comes to Him with a heart that is not sound, and the heart is God's trust with His servant. One of the gnostics said: God Most High has two secrets for His servant by way of inspiration. The first: when he comes out from his mother's womb, God says to him: "My servant, I have brought you out into the world pure and clean, and I have entrusted and deposited with you this trust, so see how you will guard the trust, and see how you will meet Me." The second: at the departure of his soul, He says: "My servant, what have you done with My trust [with you]? Have you kept it so that you meet Me upon the covenant, and I meet you with fulfillment? Or have you wasted it, so that I meet you with demand and punishment?"

Perhaps he (Abu 'Amr, or the reciter) assimilated the ta' of the tafa''ul form (ta' al-tafa''ul, the reflexive prefix) to indicate that if he delays doing this for the sake of concealment, so that it is more excellent, or its assimilation is a shortening, since the matter reaches a limit that requires brevity in speech, as was requested in the time. This is supported by the recitation of the majority, other than Abu 'Amr, ﴿and I would be﴾ with a jazm (apocopation, the jussive ending), coordinated with the response (jawab) that the context guides one to supply. For the state of this person, who has become so anxious, requires that he intended: "If You delay me, I will give charity." But he omitted it because the situation is too constrained for it and the circumstance requires its omission. This is the meaning of what Sibawayh related from al-Khalil: that the jazm is on the assumption of the conditional (shart) which the wish (tamanni) indicates by its place, since the jussive particle is not actually present. The meaning of what others said is that "lawla" (why not), because it is hortatory (tahdid), includes the meaning of a command and the meaning of a condition, so it is as if it were said: "Delay me," and its response without the fa' (the particle "fa") is jussive in form, while the one connected with fa' is jussive in position, so "wa-akun" is coordinated with the position. Abu 'Amr read it in the accusative, coordinating with the form, because it is the response to the wish that "lawla" indicates. The agreement of the codices on omitting the waw (the conjunction) does not harm this, because he said that it is for brevity, which is evident. This is because of the correspondence between the pronunciation, the writing, the time, and the intended meaning. From here you come to know the greatness of the reciters and their intent, God willing, by their saying in the well-known rule, even if it agrees with the orthography of the codex, even if only as a possibility: ﴿from the righteous﴾, meaning those who excel in this great attribute. He added to the urging to hasten to acts of obedience before they are lost by his saying, emphasizing for a great hope from this dying person, for the delay, coordinated with [what] its supposition is: "So God will not delay it, and he will miss what he intended."

(ﷺ) is not used here, so no honorific appears in this passage.

﴿And never﴾. It is also permissible for the clause to be a circumstantial clause (ḥāl, a clause describing the state of the subject), meaning: he said this while the state was that He ﴿will never delay Allah﴾, i.e. the Supreme King, for whom there is no equal, so there is no objection to Him, ﴿a soul﴾, i.e. any soul whatsoever. He confirmed the term by His saying: ﴿when its term has come﴾, i.e. the time of its death which Allah has set for it. So Allah will not delay the soul of this speaker, for it is among the souls included in the negation. Since the meaning follows the path of conclusions which the wording unquestionably guides to, namely: Allah is All-Knowing, so He says this, He followed it with His saying, urging haste in escaping the obligation of acts of obedience and in preparing for what must be met of the encounter, warning against neglect, and because nothing is as effective a threat as knowledge: ﴿And Allah﴾, i.e. the One who has comprehensive encompassment in knowledge and power, ﴿is Acquainted﴾, i.e. of utmost awareness and knowledge, outwardly and inwardly, ﴿with what you do﴾, i.e. with what you bring about of your deeds in the past, present and future, all of it, outward and inward, from this which I have informed you the disobedient dying person says, and from others [from him and from others] (p-98) O people. This is according to the recitation of the majority (qira'at al-Jumhur, the widely accepted reading) with the second person address. According to the recitation of Abu Bakr from ʿAsim, with the third person (bi-l-ghayb), it is possible that the hypocrites are intended. It is possible that it is general, so that the pronoun refers to the soul according to its meaning. It is possible that the pronoun refers to the people, by way of iltifat (a shift from one grammatical person to another) from direct address to turning away, as a warning to them. For this reason He, glory be to Him, knew the lie of the hypocrites in claiming that they believe what they testified to regarding the matter of the Messenger, and He knew all that was narrated of their reports. ﴿Does He not know who created? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾ [al-Mulk: 14]. And Allah knows best.
